literal: Concealment affliction those-without-(acc.) if-seen, poverty affliction all together will-perish.
translation: If one sees those who do not have the affliction of hiding what they have, all the afflictions of poverty will perish at once.
modern: தன்னிடம் உள்ளதை மறைத்து வைக்கும் நோய் இல்லாதவர்களைக் கண்டால், வறுமையால் வரும் துன்பங்கள் எல்லாம் ஒன்றாக அழிந்துவிடும்.
explanation: The couplet contrasts two types of suffering: the suffering of poverty and the suffering of stinginess. The word 'கரப்பு' means concealment, referring to the habit of hiding one's wealth to avoid giving to those who ask. The poet calls this an 'இடும்பை' (affliction), just as poverty ('நிரப்பு') is an affliction. When a person in need encounters someone free from the disease of withholding, all the sorrows of their poverty are destroyed at once.
